post: Shipped a focus timer that only counts minutes you actually spend in the editor. Week 12 of building one small app a week.

replies.text: Does it stop counting when you alt-tab to docs? My worst lost hours are in the browser while I tell myself it's research.
Nice, timers are always useful for this kind of thing.
Great post! Love this 🔥

post: Hot take: most startups should not have a staging environment until they have paying customers.

replies.text: We dropped staging at 3 people and used feature flags plus a Postgres branch per PR. The one thing we missed was testing migrations against prod-sized data.
Depends on the team I guess, there are tradeoffs either way.
So true!! 💯

post: We cut our CI time from 22 minutes to 6 by caching node_modules and splitting the test suite into 4 shards.

replies.text: Did sharding by file count or by past runtime? We split by file and one shard still took 3x the others because of the e2e folder.
CI speed matters a lot, good to see people working on it.
Amazing work, this is awesome!

post: I've interviewed 40 founders this year. The ones who ship fastest all write a one-page spec before they code.

replies.text: What goes on the page? I've seen one-pagers that are just a wish list. The useful ones I've used name what we will not build.
Planning is important, makes sense.
Incredible insight! Thanks for sharing 🙏

post: Our app's day-30 retention went from 8% to 19% after we removed the signup wall and let people try it first.

replies.text: Did the share of people who eventually signed up drop, or did it hold? Ours fell by a third and we still came out ahead.
Interesting result, onboarding is tricky.
Wow, this is huge! Congrats! 🎉

post: Rewrote our Python data pipeline in Rust. Runtime went from 4 hours to 11 minutes. Memory use dropped 90%.

replies.text: How much of that came from the language versus fixing the pipeline while rewriting it? Our 'Rust win' turned out to be mostly removing a pandas copy in a loop.
Rust is fast, not surprised it helped.
Game changer! Rust is the best 🚀

post: Unpopular opinion: daily standups are a waste of time for teams under 5 people.

replies.text: We replaced ours with a written note at 10am in Slack and a 15 minute call only on Mondays. Blockers now surface faster because people post them when they hit them.
Meetings in general can be a lot sometimes.
Couldn't agree more! 👏👏

post: Spent the weekend building a Raspberry Pi sensor that texts me when my plants need water.

replies.text: Which moisture sensor? The cheap resistive ones corroded in a month for me; the capacitive v1.2 has lasted a year in the same pot.
Fun weekend project, plants are hard to keep alive.
This is so cool!! Love it

post: Pricing lesson: we raised our price from $9 to $29 a month and churn went down.

replies.text: Did you grandfather existing users at $9? We didn't, lost 12% of them in the first month, and still made more because the new signups stayed longer.
Pricing is always a big question for any business.
Brilliant! Great thread 🔥🔥

post: Our open source library just passed 10k GitHub stars. Three years, two maintainers, zero funding.

replies.text: How do the two of you split issue triage? At 5k stars we were drowning until we added a template that asks for a failing test before anyone looks.
Open source is hard work, congrats on the milestone.
Congrats!! Huge milestone 🎉🎉
